title.zh: 卷444 列傳二百三十一 黄体芳 宗室宝廷 宗室盛昱 张佩伦 邓承修 徐致祥
title.en: Volume 444 Biographies 231: Huang Tifang, Zong Shibaoting, Zong Shishengyu, Zhang Peilun, Deng Chengxiu, Xu Zhixiang
title.raw: 卷444 列傳二百三十一 黄体芳 宗室宝廷 宗室盛昱 张佩伦 邓承修 徐致祥

sentences.zh: 黃體芳，字漱蘭，浙江瑞安人。

translations.literal: Huang Tifang, styled Shulan, was a native of Ruian in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Tifang, whose courtesy name was Shulan, came from Ruian in Zhejiang Province.

sentences.zh: 同治二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationer, and received appointment as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 日探討掌故，慨然有經世志。

translations.literal: Daily he investigated historical precedents and records, and with deep feeling harbored a will to order the age.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his days studying institutional history and records, and came to hold a strong desire to put his learning at the service of the state.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士，頻上書言時政得失。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Reader of the Hanlin Academy and frequently submitted memorials on the gains and losses of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted in stages to Reader of the Hanlin Academy, he often memorialized the throne on what was right and wrong in contemporary governance.

sentences.zh: 晉、豫飢，請籌急賑，整吏治，清庶獄，稱旨。

translations.literal: When Shanxi and Henan suffered famine, he requested urgent relief measures, rectification of official administration, and clearing of ordinary criminal cases; his proposals pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in Shanxi and Henan he urged emergency relief, reform of local administration, and review of routine criminal cases, and the court approved his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 時議禁燒鍋裕民食，戶部覈駁，體芳謂燒鍋領帖，部獲歲銀三萬，因上董恂奸邪狀，坐鐫級。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of banning distilleries to ease the people's food supply; the Board of Revenue rejected the proposal. Tifang said that distilleries held licenses and the Board received thirty thousand taels of silver yearly from them; he therefore submitted a memorial on Dong Xun's wickedness and was demoted one grade as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When officials debated banning liquor stills to free grain for the people, the Board of Revenue objected. Tifang pointed out that licensed stills paid the Board thirty thousand taels a year; he then memorialized against Dong Xun's corruption and was punished with a one-grade demotion.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年三月，惠陵禮成，主事吳可讀為定大統以屍諫。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year of Guangxu, when the rites for Emperor Muzong's tomb were completed, the principal clerk Wu Kedu remonstrated with his corpse to fix the succession.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1879, after the burial rites for Emperor Tongzhi were finished, Principal Clerk Wu Kedu used his own death as a memorial to demand a settled line of succession.

sentences.zh: 詔言：「同治十三年十二月初五日降旨，嗣後皇帝生有皇子，即承繼大行皇帝為嗣。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "On the fifth day of the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Tongzhi an edict was issued that whenever the emperor thereafter had a son, that son should succeed the late emperor as heir.
translations.idiomatic: The throne proclaimed: "By the edict of 5 January 1875, whenever the reigning emperor should have a son, that son is to succeed the late emperor as his heir."

sentences.zh: 吳可讀所奏，前旨即是此意。

translations.literal: What Wu Kedu memorialized accords with the meaning of the earlier edict.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kedu's petition expresses exactly what the prior edict intended.

sentences.zh: 」於是下群臣議，體芳略言：「'即是此意'一語，止有恪遵，更有何議？

translations.literal: " Thereupon the court ordered the ministers to deliberate. Tifang wrote briefly: "As for the phrase 'that is the meaning,' there is only dutiful compliance—what further is there to debate?
translations.idiomatic: The court then referred the matter to the ministers. Tifang wrote in summary: "The words 'that is the meaning' allow only reverent obedience—what more is there to argue?"

sentences.zh: 乃激烈者盛氣力爭，巽畏者囁嚅不吐，或忠或謹，皆人臣盛節，而惜其未明今日事勢也。

translations.literal: Yet the vehement contended with heated zeal, while the timid murmured and would not speak out; whether loyal or cautious, all showed the utmost integrity of subjects, yet it is a pity they did not understand today's situation.
translations.idiomatic: The impassioned fought with fierce zeal, while the timid stammered and held back; whether loyal or cautious, each showed a subject's highest integrity, yet none quite grasped the situation of the day.

sentences.zh: 譬諸士民之家，長子次子各有孫，而自祖父母視之則無異。

translations.literal: Compare it to a scholar-commoner household: the eldest and second sons each have grandsons, yet to the grandparents there is no difference.
translations.idiomatic: Think of an ordinary family: the eldest and second sons each have grandsons, yet to the grandparents they are all the same.

sentences.zh: 然襲爵職必歸之長房者，嫡長與嫡次之別也。

translations.literal: Yet the hereditary title and office must pass to the senior line—that is the distinction between the legitimate eldest son and the legitimate second son.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rank and hereditary office must go to the senior branch—that is the difference between the eldest legitimate son and the next legitimate son.

sentences.zh: 又如大宗無子，次宗止一嫡子，然小宗以嫡子繼大宗，不聞有所吝者，以仍得兼承本宗故也。

translations.literal: Again, if the major lineage has no son and the minor lineage has only one legitimate son, the minor lineage's legitimate son may succeed the major lineage without complaint, because he can still also inherit his own lineage.
translations.idiomatic: If the main line has no heir while a collateral line has a single legitimate son, that son may succeed the main line without objection, since he can still carry on his birth line as well.

sentences.zh: 唯君與民微有不同。

translations.literal: Only between ruler and subject is there a slight difference.
translations.idiomatic: Between sovereign and subject, however, the case differs slightly.

sentences.zh: 民間以嫡子繼大宗，則大宗為主，本宗為兼。

translations.literal: Among the people, when a legitimate son succeeds a major lineage, the major lineage is primary and the birth lineage secondary.
translations.idiomatic: In private life, when a legitimate son succeeds a main line, the main line is primary and the birth line secondary.

sentences.zh: 天潢以嫡子繼帝系，則帝係為主，本宗可得而兼，親不可得而兼。

translations.literal: When the imperial house uses a legitimate son to continue the imperial line, the imperial line is primary; the birth lineage may be joined but the parental bond cannot be joined.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial house continues the throne through a legitimate son, the imperial succession is primary: the birth line may be combined with it, but the tie of parent and child cannot be combined.

sentences.zh: 若人君以嫡子繼長支，則固以繼長支為主，而本宗亦不能不兼。

translations.literal: If the ruler uses a legitimate son to continue the senior branch, he must take continuing the senior branch as primary, yet the birth lineage cannot but be joined as well.
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign continues the senior branch through a legitimate son, continuing that branch is primary, yet the birth line cannot fail to be joined as well.

sentences.zh: 蓋人君無小宗，即稱謂加以區別，亦於本宗恩義無傷。

translations.literal: For the ruler has no minor lineage; even if titles are distinguished in address, the kindness and duty of the birth lineage are not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign has no minor lineage as such; even if titles are distinguished in address, the moral claims of the birth line remain intact.

sentences.zh: 此兩宮意在嗣子承統，慈愛穆宗，亦即所以慈愛皇上之說也。

translations.literal: This is the meaning of the two palaces: that the heir-son should carry on the succession, loving Emperor Muzong—and thereby also loving the present emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The two palaces meant that the heir should carry on the succession, cherishing Emperor Tongzhi—and in doing so cherishing the present emperor as well.

sentences.zh: 今非合兩統為一統，以不定為豫定，就將來承繼者以為承嗣，似亦無策以處之矣。

translations.literal: Today we must unite two successions into one, treat what is unsettled as already foreordained, and regard the future successor as the heir—otherwise there seems no policy to settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the two successions are merged into one, the unsettled treated as foreordained, and the future heir regarded as already the heir, there appears to be no workable policy.

sentences.zh: 試思此時即不專為穆宗計，既正名為先帝嗣子，豈有僅封一王貝勒者乎？

translations.literal: Consider: even if one did not think only of Muzong, once he is properly named the late emperor's heir-son, could he be given only the rank of prince or beile?
translations.idiomatic: Even setting Tongzhi aside, once the heir is formally named the late emperor's son, could he be enfeoffed merely as a prince or beile?

sentences.zh: 即不專為皇上計，古來天子之嗣子，豈有以不主神器之諸皇子當之者乎？

translations.literal: Even if one did not think only of the present emperor, in antiquity could the son of Heaven's heir be any but a prince who would hold the sacred vessel?
translations.idiomatic: Even setting the present emperor aside, when has the Son of Heaven's heir ever been anyone other than the one destined for the throne?

sentences.zh: 即僅為穆宗計，皇上可如民間出繼之子乎？

translations.literal: Even thinking only of Muzong, could the present emperor be like a commoner's adopted-out son?
translations.idiomatic: Even for Tongzhi alone, could the present emperor be treated like a son given out for adoption in a private family?

sentences.zh: 即僅為皇上計，穆宗可如前明稱為皇伯考乎？

translations.literal: Even thinking only of the present emperor, could Muzong be styled as in the Ming, "Imperial Uncle by Birth"?
translations.idiomatic: Even for the present emperor alone, could Tongzhi be addressed as the Ming styled an emperor's uncle by birth?

sentences.zh: 夫奉祖訓，禀懿旨，體聖意，非僭。

translations.literal: To follow ancestral instruction, obey the empress dowager's edict, and embody the sage emperor's intent is not presumption.
translations.idiomatic: To follow ancestral teaching, obey the empress dowager's edict, and embody the emperor's intent is not overreaching.

sentences.zh: 先帝今上皆無不宜，非悖。

translations.literal: Neither the late emperor nor the present emperor is wronged; it is not disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Neither the late emperor nor the present one is slighted; this is not disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 明其統而非其人，非擅。

translations.literal: To clarify the succession rather than the person is not usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: To clarify the line of succession rather than the person is not usurpation.

sentences.zh: 論統系，辨宗法，正足見國家億萬年無疆之庥，非干犯忌諱。

translations.literal: To discuss the succession system and distinguish clan law truly shows the boundless blessing of the state for ten thousand years; it is not to offend taboo.
translations.idiomatic: To discuss the succession and clarify clan law is precisely to show the state's blessing for ages to come; it is not to breach taboo.

sentences.zh: 此固無意氣可逞，亦無功罪可言也。

translations.literal: Here there is truly no temper to vent, nor merit or fault to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Here there is no room for personal temper, nor any merit or blame to claim.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，詔存毓慶宮。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, an edict ordered it kept in the Palace of Nurturing Joy.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was received, the court ordered it filed in the Palace of Nurturing Joy.

sentences.zh: 自是劾尚書賀壽慈飾奏，俄使崇厚誤國，洪鈞譯地圖舛謬，美使崔國英赴賽會失體，皆人所難言，直聲震中外。

translations.literal: Thereafter he impeached Minister He Shouci for embellishing memorials, soon after the Russian envoy Chonghou for harming the state, Hong Jun for errors in translating maps, and the American envoy Cui Guoying for impropriety at an exposition—all matters others dared not speak of; his forthright voice shook China and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he impeached Minister He Shouci for dressing up reports, the Russian envoy Chonghou for betraying the nation, Hong Jun for mistakes in map translation, and the American envoy Cui Guoying for impropriety at an exhibition—matters others would not touch; his blunt reputation resounded at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷內閣學士，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Grand Secretary and supervised education in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he was made Grand Secretary and appointed educational commissioner for Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 明年，授兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Left Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 中法事起，建索還琉球、經畫越南議。

translations.literal: When the Sino-French conflict arose, he proposed recovering Ryukyu and planning policy on Vietnam.
translations.idiomatic: When war with France broke out, he urged the recovery of Ryukyu and a settled policy toward Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 十一年，還京，劾李鴻章治兵無效，請敕曾紀澤遄歸練師，忤旨，左遷通政使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he returned to the capital, impeached Li Hongzhang for ineffective military administration, and asked that Zeng Jize be ordered home at once to train troops; displeasing the throne, he was demoted to Commissioner of the Court of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he returned to Beijing, impeached Li Hongzhang for failing to manage the army, and asked that Zeng Jize be recalled immediately to train forces; the court took offense and demoted him to Commissioner of the Court of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 兩署左副都御史，奏言自強之本在內治，又歷陳中外交涉得失，後卒如所言。

translations.literal: Twice acting as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, he memorialized that the foundation of self-strengthening lies in internal governance, and repeatedly set forth the gains and losses of foreign relations; events later proved him right.
translations.idiomatic: Twice acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, he argued that self-strengthening rests on internal order and repeatedly analyzed foreign affairs; later events bore him out.

sentences.zh: 十七年，乞休。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1891 he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1899.

sentences.zh: 子紹箕、紹第，並能承家學，而紹箕尤贍雅。

translations.literal: His sons Shaoji and Shaodi both could carry on the family learning, and Shaoji was especially elegant and generous.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shaoji and Shaodi both inherited the family scholarship, and Shaoji was especially refined and generous.

sentences.zh: 紹箕，字仲弢。

translations.literal: Shaoji, styled Zhongtao.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoji, whose courtesy name was Zhongtao.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年進士，以編修典試湖北。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination and, as a compiler, conducted the provincial examination in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1880 he became a jinshi and, while serving as a compiler, supervised the provincial examination in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 晉侍講，擢庶子。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Reader and then to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Reader and was then appointed Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 京師立大學堂，充總辦。

translations.literal: When the Imperial University was established in the capital, he served as chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial University was founded in Beijing, he served as its chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 究心東西邦學制，手訂章條。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to Eastern and Western educational systems and personally drafted the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Eastern and Western school systems in depth and personally drafted the university regulations.

sentences.zh: 遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 歷充編書局、譯書局監督。

translations.literal: He successively served as supervisor of the Compilation Bureau and the Translation Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as supervisor of the Compilation Bureau and the Translation Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為湖北提學使。

translations.literal: He went out as Educational Commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Educational Commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 東渡日本，與其邦人士論孔教、輒心折。

translations.literal: Crossing to Japan, he debated Confucian teaching with scholars there and was repeatedly won over.
translations.idiomatic: In Japan he debated Confucian doctrine with local scholars and was often deeply impressed by them.

sentences.zh: 歸，未幾，卒。

translations.literal: After returning, he died before long.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after his return he died.

sentences.zh: 宗室寶廷，字竹坡，隸滿洲鑲藍旗，鄭獻親王濟爾哈朗八世孫。

translations.literal: Zongshi Baoting, styled Zhupo, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and was the eighth-generation descendant of Prince Jirhalang of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Baoting of the imperial clan, courtesy name Zhupo, was of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and eighth in descent from Prince Jirhalang of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 同治七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Reader.

sentences.zh: 光緒改元，疏請選師保以崇聖德，嚴宦寺以杜干預，覈實內務府以節糜費，訓練神機營以備緩急，懿旨嘉納。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Guangxu he memorialized to select tutors to exalt the sage's virtue, strictly control eunuchs to block interference, verify the Imperial Household Department to cut waste, and train the Shenji Camp for emergencies; the empress dowager's edict praised and accepted his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangxu he urged choosing tutors to elevate the emperor's moral cultivation, tightening control over eunuchs, auditing the Imperial Household Department, and drilling the Shenji Camp; the empress dowager approved his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 大考三等，降中允，尋授司業。

translations.literal: In the great examination he received third grade, was demoted to Junior Mentor, and soon after was appointed Vice Director of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace examination he placed third class, was demoted to Junior Mentor, and soon received appointment as Vice Director of Education.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷方銳意求治，詔詢吏治民生用人行政，寶廷力抉其弊，諤諤數百言，至切直。

translations.literal: At that time the court was keen to seek good government and issued an edict inquiring into official administration, the people's livelihood, appointment of men, and governance; Baoting forcefully exposed its abuses in several hundred forthright words, to the utmost directness.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then eager for reform and asked about administration, livelihood, appointments, and policy; Baoting exposed abuses in several hundred blunt words, with utmost frankness.

sentences.zh: 晉、豫飢，應詔陳言，請罪己，並責臣工。

translations.literal: When Shanxi and Henan suffered famine, he responded to the edict with memorials asking the emperor to blame himself and also to reproach his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in Shanxi and Henan he answered the imperial call by asking the emperor to reproach himself and to hold his ministers accountable.

sentences.zh: 條上救荒四事，曰：察釐稅，開糧捐，購洋米，增糶局。

translations.literal: He listed four measures for famine relief: scrutinize tax collection, open grain contributions, purchase foreign rice, and increase government grain sales.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed four relief measures: audit tax collection, open grain-donation drives, purchase foreign rice, and expand government grain sales.

sentences.zh: 復以災廣賑劇，請行分貸法。

translations.literal: Because the disaster was wide and relief heavy, he also asked to implement a system of divided loans.
translations.idiomatic: As the disaster was widespread and relief burdens heavy, he also urged a system of divided loans.

sentences.zh: 畿輔旱，日色赤，市言訛駴，建議內嚴防範，外示鎮定，以安人心。

translations.literal: When the capital region suffered drought and the sun appeared red, rumors and panic spread in the markets; he proposed strict precautions within and a show of calm without to settle the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Drought in the metropolitan region turned the sun reddish and rumors panicked the markets; he urged tight internal precautions and outward calm to steady public feeling.

sentences.zh: 歷遷侍講學士，以六事進，曰：明黜陟，專責任，詳考詢，嚴程限，去欺矇，慎赦宥，稱旨。

translations.literal: Promoted in stages to Reader of the Hanlin Academy, he advanced six proposals: clarify promotions and demotions, fix responsibility, conduct detailed inquiries, enforce deadlines, remove deception, and be cautious with amnesties; his proposals pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Rising to Reader of the Hanlin Academy, he submitted six reforms—clarify promotion and demotion, fix responsibility, conduct thorough inquiry, enforce deadlines, remove deceit, and be cautious with amnesties—and won imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879 he was made Reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 初，德宗繼統嗣文宗，懿旨謂將來生有皇子，即繼穆宗為嗣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Dezong had succeeded to the throne as heir to Emperor Wenzong; the empress dowager's edict said that when a son should be born in future, he would succeed Emperor Muzong as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Guangxu had succeeded as heir to Emperor Xianfeng; the empress dowager's edict held that when the emperor should later have a son, that son would succeed Emperor Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 內閣侍讀學士廣安請頒鐵券，被訶責。

translations.literal: Reader of the Hanlin Academy Guang An asked that an iron certificate be issued and was rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Reader Guang An petitioned for an iron certificate of assurance and was reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 至是，穆宗奉安惠陵，主事吳可讀堅請為其立後，以屍諫，下廷臣議。

translations.literal: At this time, when Emperor Muzong was installed at Huiling, Principal Clerk Wu Kedu firmly asked that an heir be established for him and remonstrated with his corpse; the court referred the matter to the ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Now, with Tongzhi's burial at Huiling complete, Wu Kedu demanded an heir for him and used his death as a memorial; the court ordered the ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 寶廷謂：「恭繹懿旨之意，蓋言穆宗未有儲貳，即以皇上所生之子為嗣，非言生皇子即時承繼也，言嗣而統賅焉矣。

translations.literal: Baoting said: "Reverently interpreting the empress dowager's edict, it means that because Muzong had no heir, the emperor's own son should be the heir—not that whenever a son is born he should succeed at once; speaking of heir, the succession is included therein.
translations.idiomatic: Baoting wrote: "Reading the empress dowager's edict reverently, it means that because Tongzhi had no heir, the emperor's own son should be his heir—not that every newborn prince succeeds immediately; 'heir' already embraces the succession."

sentences.zh: 引伸之，蓋言將來即以皇上傳統之皇子繼穆宗為嗣也。

translations.literal: Extended further, it means that in future the emperor's son who carries on the imperial line will succeed Muzong as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Taken further, it means that the emperor's son who will carry on the throne shall in time succeed Tongzhi as heir.

sentences.zh: 因皇上甫承大統，故渾涵其詞，留待親政日自下明詔，此皇太后不忍歧視之慈心，欲以孝弟仁讓之休歸之皇上也。

translations.literal: Because the emperor had just assumed the great succession, the wording was deliberately broad, to await the day of personal rule when a clear edict would be issued; this was the empress dowager's compassionate heart unwilling to discriminate, wishing to return the blessings of filial piety, brotherly love, benevolence, and yielding to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor had only just succeeded, the language was deliberately broad, to await the day he took personal rule and issued a clear edict— the empress dowager's compassion unwilling to divide affections, wishing to leave the honor of filial piety, brotherhood, benevolence, and yielding to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 廣安不能喻，故生爭於前；

translations.literal: Guang An could not understand, and therefore contended while alive;
translations.idiomatic: Guang An failed to understand and quarreled in life;

sentences.zh: 吳可讀不能喻，故死爭於後。

translations.literal: Wu Kedu could not understand, and therefore contended in death.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kedu failed to understand and contended in death.

sentences.zh: 竊痛可讀殉死之忠，而又惜其遺摺之言不盡意也。

translations.literal: I deeply mourn Wu Kedu's loyal death, yet regret that the words of his final memorial did not fully express his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: I deeply honor Wu Kedu's martyrdom, yet regret that his final memorial did not fully express his intent.

sentences.zh: 可讀未喻懿旨言外之意，而其遺摺未達之意，皇太后早鑑及之，故曰'前降旨時即是此意'也。

translations.literal: Wu Kedu did not grasp the meaning beyond the edict's words, yet the meaning his memorial did not reach the empress dowager had long discerned; hence she said, "The earlier edict already meant this."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kedu missed the meaning beyond the edict's words, yet what his memorial left unsaid the empress dowager had long seen; hence "the earlier edict already meant this."

sentences.zh: 而可讀猶以忠佞不齊為慮，誠過慮也。

translations.literal: Yet Wu Kedu still worried that loyal and wicked ministers would not stand together—truly excessive worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wu Kedu still feared loyal and wicked ministers would not stand together—a needless anxiety.

sentences.zh: 宋太宗背杜太后，明景帝廢太子見深，雖因佞臣妄進邪說，究由二君有自私之心。

translations.literal: Song Taizong went against Empress Dowager Du, and Ming Jingdi deposed the heir apparent Zhu Jianshen; though wicked ministers advanced perverse counsel, in the end both rulers harbored selfish hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Song Taizong defied Empress Dowager Du, and Ming Jingdi deposed the heir Zhu Jianshen; though flatterers urged evil counsel, both emperors in the end acted from selfish motives.

sentences.zh: 乃者兩宮懿旨懸於上，孤臣遺疏存於下，傳之九州，載之國史，皇上天生聖人，必能以皇太后之心為心。

translations.literal: Now the two palaces' edicts hang above, and the lone minister's final memorial remains below, transmitted through the nine regions and recorded in the national histories; the emperor is a sage by nature and will surely take the empress dowager's heart as his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The two palaces' edicts hang above and the lone minister's last memorial below, spread through the realm and written into history; the emperor is a born sage and will take the empress dowager's heart as his own.

sentences.zh: 請將前後懿旨恭呈御覽，明降諭旨，宣示中外，俾天下後世咸知我皇太后至慈，皇上至孝至弟至仁至讓，且以見穆宗至聖至明，付託得人也。

translations.literal: I ask that the earlier and later edicts be respectfully presented for imperial review, that a clear edict be issued and proclaimed at home and abroad, so that all under heaven and in later ages may know our empress dowager's utmost kindness and the emperor's utmost filial piety, brotherly love, benevolence, and yielding—and also see Emperor Muzong's utmost sagacity and clarity in entrusting the right man.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the earlier and later edicts be presented for review, that a clear edict be proclaimed at home and abroad, so that all ages may know the empress dowager's utmost kindness and the emperor's utmost filial piety, brotherhood, benevolence, and yielding—and see Tongzhi's sagacity in choosing the right successor.

sentences.zh: 如是，則綱紀正，名分定，天理順，人情安矣。

translations.literal: If so, then discipline is correct, titles settled, heavenly principle accorded, and human feeling at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Then ritual order is right, titles fixed, principle aligned, and feeling at peace.

sentences.zh: 因赴內閣集議，意微不合，謹以上聞。

translations.literal: Because at the Grand Council deliberation opinions differed slightly, I respectfully report the above.
translations.idiomatic: Finding slight disagreement at the Grand Council deliberation, I respectfully report the above.

translations.literal: Close of memorial quotation.
translations.idiomatic: End of memorial quotation.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「廷臣謂穆宗繼統之議，已賅於皇太后前降懿旨之中，將來神器所歸，皇上自能斟酌盡善，固也。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The court ministers say the question of Muzong's succession is already included in the empress dowager's earlier edict, and that in future the sacred vessel will fall where the emperor himself can weigh all and choose well—indeed.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Ministers say Tongzhi's succession is already covered by the empress dowager's edict, and that in future the throne will go where the emperor can weigh all and choose wisely—so they hold."

sentences.zh: 然懿旨意深詞簡，不及此引伸明晰，異日皇上生有皇子，將繼穆宗為嗣乎，抑不即繼乎？

translations.literal: Yet the edict's meaning is deep and its words brief; without this extended clarification, when the emperor later has a son, will he succeed Muzong as heir, or not succeed at once?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the edict is deep in meaning and brief in wording; without this clarification, when the emperor later has a son, will that son succeed Tongzhi at once or not?

sentences.zh: 不即繼似違懿旨，即繼又嫌跡近建儲。

translations.literal: Not succeeding at once seems to violate the edict; succeeding at once seems too close to establishing an heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Not succeeding at once seems to breach the edict; succeeding at once looks too like naming an heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 就令僅言繼嗣，不標繼統之名，而臣民亦隱以儲貳視之，是不建之建也。

translations.literal: Even if one speaks only of succeeding as heir without labeling succession to the line, the officials and people will still privately regard him as heir apparent—that is establishing an heir without establishing one.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one speaks only of heirship without naming succession to the line, officials and people will still treat him as heir apparent—an heir apparent established without being established.

sentences.zh: 而此皇子賢也，固宗社福；

translations.literal: If this prince is worthy, it is indeed the fortune of the altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: If that prince proves worthy, the realm is blessed;

sentences.zh: 如其不賢，將來仍傳繼統乎，抑舍而別傳乎？

translations.literal: if he is not worthy, in future will the succession still be transmitted, or set aside for another transmission?
translations.idiomatic: if unworthy, will the succession still pass to him, or be set aside for another line?

sentences.zh: 別傳之皇子，仍繼穆宗為嗣乎，抑不繼乎？

translations.literal: Will the prince of another transmission still succeed Muzong as heir, or not?
translations.idiomatic: Would a prince from another line still succeed Tongzhi, or not?

sentences.zh: 即使仍繼穆宗，是亦不廢立之廢立也，豈太平盛事乎？

translations.literal: Even if he still succeeds Muzong, that is deposing and establishing without deposing and establishing—how is that a great peace?
translations.idiomatic: Even if he still succeeded Tongzhi, that would be deposition and installation without calling it so—what great peace is that?

sentences.zh: 至此時即欲皇上斟酌盡善，不亦難乎？

translations.literal: At that point, even if one wished the emperor to weigh all and choose well, would it not be difficult?
translations.idiomatic: By then, even if the emperor wished to weigh all and choose wisely, would it not be hard?

sentences.zh: 廷議之意，或以皇上親政，皇子應尚未生，不難豫酌一盡善之規。

translations.literal: The court deliberation seems to think that when the emperor takes personal rule the prince will not yet be born, and it will not be hard to plan a perfect rule in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion seems to assume that when the emperor takes personal rule no prince will yet be born, so a perfect plan can easily be made in advance.

sentences.zh: 然國君十五而生子，皇子誕育如在徹簾之前，又何以處之乎？

translations.literal: Yet a ruler may beget a son at fifteen; if a prince is born before the curtain is withdrawn, how is that to be handled?
translations.idiomatic: Yet rulers may father sons at fifteen; if a prince is born before the regency ends, what then?

sentences.zh: 與其留此兩難之局以待皇上，何如及今斟酌盡善乎？

translations.literal: Rather than leave this dilemma for the emperor, why not weigh all and choose well today?
translations.idiomatic: Rather than leave this dilemma for the emperor, why not settle it wisely now?

sentences.zh: 且懿旨非皇上可改，此時不引伸明晰，將來皇上雖斟酌盡善，何敢自為變通乎？

translations.literal: Moreover the edict is not something the emperor may alter; if it is not clarified by extension now, in future even if the emperor weighs all and chooses well, how would he dare change it on his own?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the edict is not the emperor's to alter; without clarifying it now, how could he later dare change it even with the best judgment?

sentences.zh: 此未妥者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first point not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first unsettled point.

sentences.zh: 廷議又謂繼統與建儲，文義似殊，而事體則一，似也。

translations.literal: The court deliberation also says that succeeding to the line and establishing an heir apparent differ in wording but are one in substance—so it seems.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion also says succession to the line and establishing an heir differ in wording but are one in substance—or so it seems.

sentences.zh: 然列聖垂訓，原言嗣統之常，今則事屬創局，可讀意在存穆宗之統，與無故擅請建儲者有間，文義之殊，不待言矣。

translations.literal: Yet the instructions of successive sage emperors speak of the regular rule of heir and succession; today the matter is unprecedented. Wu Kedu's intent was to preserve Muzong's line, unlike those who rashly ask to establish an heir without cause—the difference in wording needs no saying.
translations.idiomatic: Yet successive emperors taught the regular rule of heir and succession; today the case is unprecedented. Wu Kedu meant to preserve Tongzhi's line, unlike those who rashly demand an heir— the verbal difference needs no argument.

sentences.zh: 今廷議不分別詞意，漫謂我朝家法未能深知，則日前懿旨'即是此意'之謂何，臣民不更滋疑乎？

translations.literal: Now the court debate does not distinguish the wording and vaguely says our dynasty's family law is not deeply known—then what of the edict's "that is the meaning"? Will not officials and people grow more doubtful?
translations.idiomatic: Now the debate ignores the distinction and vaguely claims our family law is not understood—then what of the edict's "that is the meaning"? Will not doubt only deepen?

sentences.zh: 此未妥者又一也。

translations.literal: This is the second point not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second unsettled point.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，詔藏毓慶宮。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, an edict ordered it kept in the Palace of Nurturing Joy.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was received, the court ordered it filed in the Palace of Nurturing Joy.

sentences.zh: 其他，俄使來議約，朝鮮請通商，均有所獻納。

translations.literal: On other matters, when the Russian envoy came to negotiate a treaty and Korea asked for commercial relations, he also offered proposals.
translations.idiomatic: On other matters—the Russian envoy's treaty talks and Korea's request for trade—he likewise offered recommendations.

sentences.zh: 七年，授內閣學士，出典福建鄉試。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Grand Secretary and went out to conduct the Fujian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he was made Grand Secretary and sent to supervise the Fujian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 既蕆事，還朝，以在途納妾自劾罷，築室西山，往居之。

translations.literal: When the examination duties were finished he returned to court, impeached himself and resigned for taking a concubine on the journey, built a house on the Western Hills, and went to live there.
translations.idiomatic: After completing the examination he returned to the capital, resigned on his own motion for having taken a concubine en route, built a house on the Western Hills, and retired there.

sentences.zh: 是冬，皇太后萬壽祝嘏，賞三品秩。

translations.literal: That winter, for the empress dowager's birthday felicitations, he was granted third-rank standing.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the empress dowager's birthday celebration, he was granted third-rank standing.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1890.

sentences.zh: 子壽富，庶吉士。

translations.literal: His son Shoufu was a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shoufu served as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 庚子，拳匪亂，殉難，自有傳。

translations.literal: In the gengzi year, during the Boxer turmoil, he died for the state; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, during the Boxer uprising, he died in service to the state and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 宗室盛昱，字伯熙，隸滿洲鑲白旗，肅武親王豪格七世孫。

translations.literal: Zongshi Shengyu, styled Boxi, belonged to the Manchu Bordered White Banner and was the seventh-generation descendant of Prince Hooge of Suwu.
translations.idiomatic: Shengyu of the imperial clan, courtesy name Boxi, was of the Manchu Bordered White Banner and seventh in descent from Prince Hooge of Suwu.

sentences.zh: 祖敬徵，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jingzheng was a Grand Councilor Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jingzheng served as Grand Councilor Assistant.

sentences.zh: 父恆恩，左副都御史。

translations.literal: His father Hengen was Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hengen was Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 盛昱少慧，十歲時作詩用「特勤」字，據唐闕特勤碑證新唐書突厥「純特勒」為「特勤」之誤，繇是顯名。

translations.literal: Shengyu was clever from youth; at ten he used the character "Teqin" in a poem and, citing the Tang Que Teqin stele, proved that the New Tang History's Turkic "Chun Tele" was an error for "Teqin," and thereby became famous.
translations.idiomatic: Shengyu was precocious; at ten he used the term Teqin in verse and, citing the Tang Que Teqin stele, showed the New Tang History's Turkic Chun Tele was a mistake for Teqin, and won renown.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年進士，既，授編修，益厲學，討測經史、輿地及本朝掌故，皆能詳其沿革。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination; once appointed compiler, he redoubled his studies, investigating classics, history, geography, and the institutions of the present dynasty, all in detailed evolution.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he became a jinshi; appointed compiler, he threw himself into study of the classics, history, geography, and Qing institutions, tracing each in detail.

sentences.zh: 累遷右庶子，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Junior Mentor and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Junior Mentor and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder.

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督何璟、巡撫劉秉璋收降台匪黃金滿，盛昱劾璟等長惡養奸，請下吏嚴議，發金滿黑龍江、新疆安置。

translations.literal: When Fujian-Zhejiang Governor He Jing and Provincial Governor Liu Bingzhang accepted the surrender of Taiwan bandit Huang Jinman, Shengyu impeached them for nurturing wickedness and pleaded for strict punishment; Jinman was sent to Heilongjiang and Xinjiang for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: When Governors He Jing and Liu Bingzhang accepted the surrender of Taiwan bandit Huang Jinman, Shengyu impeached them for harboring evil and urged severe punishment; Jinman was exiled to Heilongjiang and Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 尚書彭玉麟數辭官不受職，劾其自便身圖，啟功臣驕蹇之漸。

translations.literal: Minister Peng Yulin repeatedly resigned office and would not accept appointment; Shengyu impeached him for seeking his own ease and opening the way for meritorious ministers' arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Peng Yulin repeatedly refused office, Shengyu impeached him for self-convenience and encouraging the arrogance of meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 浙江按察使陳寶箴陛見未行，追論官河南聽獄不慎，罷免；

translations.literal: Zhejiang Surveillance Commissioner Chen Baozhen had not yet departed on his audience with the throne when Shengyu pursued charges of careless handling of cases while he was in Henan and secured his dismissal;
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhejiang Surveillance Commissioner Chen Baozhen could depart for his audience, Shengyu revived charges of mishandled cases in Henan and secured his dismissal;

sentences.zh: 張佩綸劾其留京幹進，寶箴疏辯，盛昱言其嘵嘵失大臣體，請再下吏議。

translations.literal: Zhang Peilun impeached him for lingering in the capital to seek advancement; Chen memorialized in defense, and Shengyu said his clamor lacked the bearing of a great minister and asked that he be referred again for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Peilun impeached him for lingering in the capital to seek advancement; when Chen defended himself, Shengyu said his clamor lacked a senior minister's dignity and asked a second inquiry.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮之亂也，提督吳長慶奉北洋大臣張樹聲檄，率師入朝，執大院君李罡應以歸，時詫為奇勳。

translations.literal: When Korea was in turmoil, Brigadier Wu Changqing, by order of Beiyang Minister Zhang Shusheng, led troops into Korea and brought back the Grand Prince Li Gangying—a feat then hailed as a singular merit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Korean crisis, Brigadier Wu Changqing entered Korea under Zhang Shusheng's orders and brought back Grand Prince Li Gangying, then hailed as a brilliant exploit.

sentences.zh: 盛昱言：「出自誘劫，不足言功，徒令屬國寒心，友邦騰笑。

translations.literal: Shengyu said: "It sprang from enticement and seizure and is not worth calling merit; it only makes the tributary state lose heart and foreign powers laugh.
translations.idiomatic: Shengyu wrote: "This came of enticement and abduction, not merit; it only chills our tributary and makes foreign powers laugh."

sentences.zh: 宜嚴予處分，俾中外知非朝廷本意。

translations.literal: Strict punishment should be imposed so that at home and abroad all may know it was not the court's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Strict punishment should follow so all may know this was not the court's intent."

sentences.zh: 」為講官未半載，數言事，士論推為謇諤。

translations.literal: " Having been lecturer less than half a year, he spoke repeatedly on affairs; public opinion ranked him among the blunt remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: As lecturer less than half a year, he spoke often on public affairs; opinion ranked him among the blunt remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷祭酒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he was made Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 法越構釁，徐延旭'唐炯坐失地逮問，盛昱言：「逮問疆臣而不明降諭旨，二百年來無此政體。

translations.literal: When France and Vietnam clashed, Xu Yanxu and Tang Jiong were arrested and questioned for losing territory; Shengyu said: "To arrest frontier ministers without a clear edict—there has been no such constitutional form in two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: When France and Vietnam clashed, Xu Yanxu and Tang Jiong were arrested for losing territory; Shengyu said: "To seize frontier ministers without a clear edict has no precedent in two hundred years."

sentences.zh: 」並劾樞臣怠職。

translations.literal: " He also impeached the Grand Council for neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached the Grand Council for neglect.

sentences.zh: 太后怒，罷恭親王奕訢等，而詔醇親王奕枻入樞府，盛昱復言：「醇親王分地綦崇，不宜嬰以政務。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was angry and dismissed Prince Gong Yixin and others, ordering Prince Chun Yixuan into the Grand Council; Shengyu again said: "Prince Chun's territorial standing is exalted and he should not be burdened with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager dismissed Prince Gong Yixin and others and put Prince Chun Yixuan on the Grand Council; Shengyu urged that Prince Chun's exalted standing should not be burdened with routine state affairs.

sentences.zh: 」其夏，命廷臣會議和戰大局，盛昱主速戰，力陳七利，謂：「再失事機，噬臍無及。

translations.literal: That summer, when the court ordered ministers to deliberate the overall question of war and peace, Shengyu urged swift war and forcefully set forth seven advantages, saying: "If the opportunity is lost again, there will be no remedy.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when ministers were ordered to debate war and peace, Shengyu urged swift war and listed seven advantages, warning: "Miss the moment again and regret will be useless."

translations.literal: Close of memorial quotation.
translations.idiomatic: End of memorial quotation.

sentences.zh: 盛昱為祭酒，與司業治麟究心教士之法，大治學舍，加膏火，定積分日程，懲遊惰，獎樸學，士習為之一變。

translations.literal: As Director, Shengyu and Vice Director Zhi Lin devoted themselves to methods of educating scholars, greatly improved the academy buildings, increased stipends, fixed schedules for accumulated credits, punished idleness, rewarded solid learning, and student habits changed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: As Director, Shengyu and Vice Director Zhi Lin reformed teaching, improved the academy, increased stipends, fixed credit schedules, punished idleness, rewarded solid learning, and student habits changed markedly.

sentences.zh: 十四年，典試山東。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he conducted the Shandong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1888 he supervised the Shandong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年，引疾歸。

translations.literal: The next year he returned home on plea of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 盛昱家居有清譽，承學之士以得接言論風采為幸。

translations.literal: At home Shengyu enjoyed a reputation for integrity; scholars who inherited the tradition counted it fortunate to hear his words and manner.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he kept a reputation for integrity; scholars prized contact with his conversation and bearing.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1899.

sentences.zh: 張佩綸，字幼樵，直隸豐潤人。

translations.literal: Zhang Peilun, styled Youqiao, was a native of Fengrun in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Peilun, courtesy name Youqiao, came from Fengrun in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 父印塘，官安徽按察使，卒於軍。

translations.literal: His father Yintang served as Anhui Surveillance Commissioner and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yintang was Anhui Surveillance Commissioner and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 佩綸，成同治十年進士，以編脩大考擢侍講，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: Peilun passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Tongzhi, was promoted from compiler in the great examination to Reader, and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Peilun became a jinshi in 1871, rose from compiler to Reader after the palace examination, and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder.

sentences.zh: 時外侮亟，累疏陳經國大政，請敕新疆、東三省、台灣嚴戒備，杜日、俄窺伺。

translations.literal: As foreign aggression pressed, he repeatedly memorialized on great policies of ordering the state, asking that Xinjiang, the Northeast, and Taiwan be strictly guarded against Japanese and Russian covetousness.
translations.idiomatic: As foreign pressure mounted, he repeatedly memorialized on statecraft, urging strict defense of Xinjiang, the Northeast, and Taiwan against Japanese and Russian designs.

sentences.zh: 晉、豫飢，畿輔旱，乃引祖宗成訓，請上下交儆，條四目以進：曰誠祈，曰集議，曰恤民，曰省刑。

translations.literal: When Shanxi and Henan suffered famine and the capital region drought, he cited ancestral precedents and asked that court and country alike take warning, advancing four items: sincere prayer, collective deliberation, cherishing the people, and reducing punishments.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in Shanxi and Henan and drought around the capital, he cited ancestral precedent and urged court and realm to take warning, proposing sincere prayer, collective deliberation, cherishing the people, and reducing punishments.

sentences.zh: 恭親王奕訢遭讒構，復請責王竭誠負重，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: Prince Gong Yixin had suffered slander; Peilun again asked that the prince be charged to serve with full loyalty and heavy responsibility; the throne praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Gong Yixin fell victim to slander, Peilun asked that he be charged to serve loyally with full responsibility; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 通政使黃體芳繼陳災狀，語稍激，絓吏議，佩綸力爭，被宥。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Court of Transmission Huang Tifang next described the disaster in heated language and was caught in an official inquiry; Peilun argued forcefully and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Tifang described the disaster in heated language and faced official inquiry, Peilun argued forcefully and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 尋丁憂，服竟，起故官。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning; when mourning ended he resumed his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning; when it ended he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 時琉球已亡，法圖越南亟，佩綸曰：「亡琉球則朝鮮可危，棄越南則緬甸必失。

translations.literal: At that time Ryukyu had perished and France was pressing on Vietnam; Peilun said: "If Ryukyu is lost, Korea is in danger; if Vietnam is abandoned, Burma will surely be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Ryukyu had fallen and France was pressing Vietnam; Peilun warned: "Lose Ryukyu and Korea is endangered; abandon Vietnam and Burma will follow."

sentences.zh: 」因請建置南北海防，設水師四大鎮；

translations.literal: " He therefore asked to establish northern and southern coastal defenses and set up four great naval commands;
translations.idiomatic: He urged coastal defenses north and south and four great naval commands;

sentences.zh: 又薦道員徐延旭、唐炯知兵堪任邊事，其招致劉永福黑旗兵為己用。

translations.literal: he also recommended Circuit Intendants Xu Yanxu and Tang Jiong as knowing warfare and fit for frontier affairs, and as having recruited Liu Yongfu's Black Flag Army for their own use.
translations.idiomatic: he also recommended Xu Yanxu and Tang Jiong as knowing war and fit for the frontier, and as having enlisted Liu Yongfu's Black Flag Army.

sentences.zh: 是時吳大澂、陳寶琛好論時政，與寶廷、鄧承修輩號「清流黨」，而佩綸尤以糾彈大臣著一時。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Dacheng, Chen Baochen, and others liked to discuss current affairs; with Baoting, Deng Chengxiu, and the like they were called the "Pure Stream Party," while Peilun was especially known for impeaching great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dacheng, Chen Baochen, and others then debated policy; with Baoting and Deng Chengxiu they were called the Pure Stream Party, while Peilun was especially famed for impeaching senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 如侍郎賀壽慈，尚書萬青藜、董恂，皆被劾去。

translations.literal: Such as Vice Minister He Shouci and Ministers Wan Qingli and Dong Xun—all were impeached and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister He Shouci and Ministers Wan Qingli and Dong Xun were among those impeached and driven out.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，雲南報銷案起，王文韶以樞臣掌戶部，臺諫爭上其受賕狀，上方意任隆密，乃援乾隆朝梁詩正還家侍父事，請令引嫌乞養，不報；

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu the Yunnan accounts case arose; Wang Wenshao, as a Grand Councilor, also controlled the Board of Revenue; censors competed to memorial his taking bribes while the throne deeply trusted him, and they cited the Qianlong case of Liang Shizheng returning home to serve his father, asking that he withdraw on grounds of conflict of interest and beg to nurture his parent—the request was not granted;
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 the Yunnan accounts scandal arose; Wang Wenshao sat on the Grand Council while heading the Board of Revenue; censors charged bribery though the throne trusted him deeply; citing Qianlong's Liang Shizheng precedent they asked him to withdraw for conflict of interest—without success;

sentences.zh: 又兩疏劾之，遂罷文韶，而擢佩緰署左副都御史，晉侍講學士。

translations.literal: after two more memorials impeaching him, Wenshao was dismissed and Peilun was appointed acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: after two further impeachments Wenshao was dismissed and Peilun was made acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 明年，法越構釁，佩綸章十數上，朝廷始遣兵徵土寇、綴敵勢，法人不便其所，佯議和，而陰使人攻陷南定。

translations.literal: The next year France and Vietnam clashed; Peilun submitted more than ten memorials before the court sent troops to suppress local bandits and check the enemy, and the French, finding it inconvenient, feigned peace talks while secretly attacking and taking Nanding.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as France and Vietnam clashed, Peilun submitted more than ten memorials before the court sent troops against local rebels to check the French; the French, finding this inconvenient, feigned peace while secretly taking Nanding.

sentences.zh: 佩綸請乘法兵未集，敕粵督遣水越都，而樞臣狃和局，慮佩綸梗議，令往陝西按事。

translations.literal: Peilun asked that while French forces were not yet gathered, the Guangdong governor be ordered to send troops south of the capital; but the Grand Council clung to peace and feared Peilun would obstruct agreement, and ordered him to Shaanxi on inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Peilun urged striking before French forces gathered and sending Guangdong troops south; the Grand Council clung to peace, feared his obstruction, and sent him to inspect Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 已而法果襲順化，脅越與盟，越事益壞。

translations.literal: Before long France attacked Shunhua and forced Vietnam into alliance; the Vietnamese situation worsened.
translations.idiomatic: France soon attacked Shunhua and forced Vietnam into alliance; the situation worsened.

sentences.zh: 使歸，命在總理各國事務衙門行走。

translations.literal: On his return he was ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 十年，法人聲內犯，佩綸謂越難未已，黑旗猶存，萬無分兵東來理，請毋罷戍啟戎心，上韙之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the French threatened invasion inland; Peilun said the Vietnamese difficulty was not ended and the Black Flags still survived, so there was no reason they would divide forces eastward, and asked that garrisons not be withdrawn lest warlike intent be aroused; the throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884, as the French threatened inland attack, Peilun argued Vietnam was unsettled and the Black Flags remained, so they would not divide forces eastward, and urged keeping garrisons; the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔就李鴻章議，遂決戰，令以三品卿銜會辦福建海疆事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered consultation with Li Hongzhang, and war was decided; Peilun was given third-rank ministerial rank to assist in Fujian coastal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court consulted Li Hongzhang and chose war; Peilun received third-rank ministerial rank to oversee Fujian coastal affairs.

sentences.zh: 佩綸至船廠，環十一艘自衛，各管帶白非計，斥之。

translations.literal: Peilun reached the shipyard, surrounded himself with eleven vessels for self-defense, and when each commander said it was not in the plan, he rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: At the shipyard Peilun surrounded himself with eleven vessels; when commanders said this was not the plan, he rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 法艦集，戰書至，眾聞警，謁佩綸亟請備，仍叱出。

translations.literal: When the French fleet assembled and a challenge arrived, on hearing the alarm the crowd came to Peilun urgently asking preparation; he still drove them out.
translations.idiomatic: When the French fleet gathered and sent a challenge, men rushed to urge preparation; he still drove them away.

sentences.zh: 比見法艦升火，始大怖，遣學生魏瀚往乞緩，未至而砲聲作，所部五營潰，其三營殲焉。

translations.literal: Only when he saw the French ships raise steam did great terror arise; he sent student Wei Han to beg delay, but before he arrived the guns sounded, his five camps collapsed, and three camps were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Only when French ships raised steam did panic set in; he sent student Wei Han to beg delay, but before arrival the guns fired, five camps collapsed, and three were annihilated.

sentences.zh: 佩綸遁鼓山麓，鄉人拒之，曰：「我會辦大臣也！

translations.literal: Peilun fled to the foot of Drum Mountain; the villagers refused him, saying: "I am the minister in charge!
translations.idiomatic: Peilun fled to Drum Mountain; villagers refused him, saying: "I am the minister in charge!"

sentences.zh: 」拒如初。

translations.literal: " They refused as before.
translations.idiomatic: They still refused him.

sentences.zh: 翼日，逃至彭田鄉，猶飾詞入告，朝旨發帑犒之，命兼船政。

translations.literal: The next day he fled to Pengtian village and still embellished his words in reports; the court ordered treasury funds to comfort him and appointed him also to the ship administration.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he fled to Pengtian village and still dressed up his reports; the court sent treasury funds to comfort him and added ship administration to his duties.

sentences.zh: 嗣聞馬尾敗，止奪卿銜，下吏議。

translations.literal: On hearing of the defeat at Mawei, only his ministerial rank was stripped and he was referred for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mawei defeat became known, only his ministerial rank was stripped and he was referred for judgment.

sentences.zh: 閩人憤甚，於是編修潘炳年、給事中萬培因等先後上其罪狀。

translations.literal: The people of Fujian were deeply angry; Compiler Pan Bingnian, Censor Wan Peiyin, and others successively memorialized his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian was furious; Compiler Pan Bingnian, Censor Wan Peiyin, and others memorialized his crimes.

sentences.zh: 時已坐薦唐尚、徐延旭褫職，至是再論戍。

translations.literal: He had already been punished for recommending Tang and Xu and losing office; now he was again sentenced to banishment.
translations.idiomatic: He had already lost office for recommending Tang Jiong and Xu Yanxu; now he was sentenced to banishment again.

sentences.zh: 居邊釋還，鴻章再延入幕，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Released from exile on the frontier, Hongzhang again invited him into his staff and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Released from frontier exile, Li Hongzhang took him into his staff again and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 甲什戰事起，御史端良劾其乾預公事，命遂回籍。

translations.literal: When the Jiawu war arose, Censor Duan Liang impeached him for interfering in public affairs and he was ordered to return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-Japanese War broke out, Censor Duan Liang impeached him for meddling in public affairs and he was ordered home.

sentences.zh: 庚子議和，鴻章薦其諳交涉，詔以編佐辦和約。

translations.literal: At the Boxer settlement Hongzhang recommended him as versed in negotiations and an edict ordered him to assist in drafting the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: At the Boxer settlement Li Hongzhang recommended him for negotiations and the court ordered him to help draft the treaty.

sentences.zh: 既成，擢四五品京堂，稱疾不出。

translations.literal: When it was finished he was promoted to fourth- or fifth-rank capital official but pleaded illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When it was done he was promoted to a fourth- or fifth-rank capital post but pleaded illness and did not serve.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1908.

sentences.zh: 何如璋，字子瓘，籍廣東大埔。

translations.literal: He Ruguan, styled Zijin, was registered in Dapu, Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruguan, courtesy name Zijin, was registered in Dapu, Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 同治七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 以侍讀出使日本。

translations.literal: As Reader he was sent as envoy to Japan.
translations.idiomatic: As Reader he was dispatched as envoy to Japan.

sentences.zh: 歸，授少詹事，出督船政。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Junior Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and went out to supervise ship administration.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made Junior Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and sent to supervise the shipyard.

sentences.zh: 承鴻章旨，狃和議，敵至，猶嚴諭各艦毋妄動。

translations.literal: Following Hongzhang's intent, he clung to peace talks; when the enemy arrived he still sternly ordered each vessel not to act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Following Li Hongzhang, he clung to peace; when the enemy came he still ordered each ship not to act rashly.

sentences.zh: 及敗，藉口押銀出奔，所如勿納，不得已，往就佩綸彭田鄉。

translations.literal: After defeat he excused himself by saying he was escorting silver and fled; wherever he went he was not admitted, and in the end he had no choice but to go to Peilun's Pengtian village.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat he claimed he was escorting silver and fled; nowhere would admit him, and he had to seek Peilun at Pengtian village.

sentences.zh: 佩綸慮敵踪跡及之，紿如璋出。

translations.literal: Peilun feared the enemy would track him there and deceived Ruguan into leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Peilun feared the enemy would follow and tricked Ruguan into leaving.

sentences.zh: 士論謂閩事之壞，佩綸為罪魁，如璋次之。

translations.literal: Public opinion said that in the Fujian disaster Peilun was the chief culprit and Ruguan second.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held Peilun the chief culprit in Fujian's disaster and Ruguan second.

sentences.zh: 如璋亦遣戍。

translations.literal: Ruguan was also banished.
translations.idiomatic: Ruguan was also banished.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家。

translations.literal: He later died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home.

sentences.zh: 鄧承修，字鐵香，廣東歸善人。

translations.literal: Deng Chengxiu, styled Tiexiang, was a native of Guishan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chengxiu, courtesy name Tiexiang, came from Guishan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 舉咸豐十一年鄉試，入貲為郎，分刑部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng he passed the provincial examination, purchased office as a secretary, and was assigned to the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he passed the provincial examination, bought office as a secretary, and was assigned to the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 轉御史，遭憂歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and returned home on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He became a censor and returned home on mourning.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu, when mourning ended, he resumed his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu, when mourning ended, he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 與張佩綸等主持清議，多彈擊，號曰「鐵漢」。

translations.literal: With Zhang Peilun and others he led the Pure Stream faction, impeaching frequently, and was called the "Iron Han."
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Peilun and others he led the Pure Stream faction, impeaching often, and was called the Iron Han.

sentences.zh: 先後疏論闈姓賭捐，大乖政體；

translations.literal: He successively memorialized on the surname lottery and gambling contributions in the examinations, greatly at odds with proper administration;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized against surname lotteries and gambling contributions in examinations as grave abuses;

sentences.zh: 關稅侵蝕，嬰害庫帑；

translations.literal: on customs duties eroded and harming the treasury;
translations.idiomatic: against customs erosion harming the treasury;

sentences.zh: 以考場積弊，陳七事糾正之；

translations.literal: on accumulated abuses in the examination halls, setting forth seven items for correction;
translations.idiomatic: on examination abuses, listing seven reforms;

sentences.zh: 吏治積弊，陳八事肅澄之。

translations.literal: and on accumulated abuses in official administration, setting forth eight items for purification.
translations.idiomatic: and on official abuses, listing eight purifications.

sentences.zh: 又劾總督李瀚章失政，左副都御史崇勳無行，侍郎長敘等違制，學政吳寶恕、葉大焯，布政使方大湜、龔易圖，鹽運使周星譽諸不職狀。

translations.literal: He also impeached Governor Li Hanzhang for maladministration, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Chongxun for misconduct, Vice Minister Chang Xu and others for violating regulations, Educational Commissioners Wu Baoshu and Ye Dachao, Provincial Administration Commissioners Fang Dashen and Gong Yitu, and Salt Transport Commissioner Zhou Xingyu for incompetence.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Governor Li Hanzhang, Left Vice Censor Chongxun, Vice Minister Chang Xu, educational commissioners Wu Baoshu and Ye Dachao, administration commissioners Fang Dashen and Gong Yitu, and salt commissioner Zhou Xingyu for misconduct or incompetence.

sentences.zh: 會邊警，糾彈舉朝慢弛，請召還左宗棠柄國政。

translations.literal: When frontier alarms arose he impeached the whole court for slackness and asked that Zuo Zongtang be recalled to direct state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier alarms arose he impeached the court's slackness and asked that Zuo Zongtang be recalled to govern.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，彗星見，則又言宗棠蒞事數月，未見設施，而因推及寶鋆、王文韶之昏眊，請罷斥，回天意。

translations.literal: A year later a comet appeared; he then said Zongtang had been in office months without visible achievement, and extended this to Baojun and Wang Wenshao's dimness, asking dismissal to turn back heaven's mind.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when a comet appeared, he said Zongtang had achieved nothing in months and extended the charge to Baojun and Wang Wenshao's incompetence, asking dismissal to appease heaven.

sentences.zh: 是時文韶方鄉用，權任轉重，會雲南報銷案起，又嚴劾之，仍不允。

translations.literal: At that time Wenshao was being promoted and his power grew heavier; when the Yunnan accounts case arose he impeached him again sternly, still without success.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao was then rising in favor; when the Yunnan accounts case arose he impeached him again, still without success.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷給事中。

translations.literal: After long service he was transferred to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was made Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時朝鮮亂平，琉球案未結，上言簡知兵大臣駐煙台，厚集南北洋戰艦番巡，留吳長慶軍戍朝互犄角。

translations.literal: When Korea was pacified and the Ryukyu case unsettled, he said a knowledgeable military minister should be stationed at Yantai, northern and southern fleets should patrol in strength, and Wu Changqing's army should remain in Korea as a mutual check.
translations.idiomatic: When Korea was pacified but Ryukyu unsettled, he urged a military minister at Yantai, strong naval patrols, and Wu Changqing's army kept in Korea as a check.

sentences.zh: 越南亂作，法人襲順化，復請詔百官廷議定國是，皆不報。

translations.literal: When Vietnam was in turmoil and the French attacked Shunhua, he again asked that the court summon all officials to deliberate national policy—all without response.
translations.idiomatic: When Vietnam erupted and France took Shunhua, he again asked a court debate on national policy—all unanswered.

sentences.zh: 十年，越事益壞，首劾徐延旭、唐炯失地喪師，趙沃、黃桂蘭擁兵僨事，宜肅國憲。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, as the Vietnamese situation worsened, he first impeached Xu Yanxu, Tang Jiong, Zhao Wo, and Huang Guilan for losing territory, wasting troops, and bungling command, asking that state law be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884, as Vietnam worsened, he first impeached Xu Yanxu, Tang Jiong, Zhao Wo, and Huang Guilan for losing territory and bungling command, urging punishment under state law.

sentences.zh: 其夏，法人原媾和，承修聯合臺諫上書，極言和議難恃。

translations.literal: That summer the French originally sought peace; Chengxiu joined censors in memorializing that peace talks could not be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, as France feigned peace, Chengxiu joined censors in warning that treaties could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 旋與司業潘衍桐密上間敵五策，並劾李鴻章定和之疏，嫉劉永福敢戰，言之憤絕。

translations.literal: Soon he and Vice Director Pan Yantong secretly submitted five stratagems against the enemy and impeached Li Hongzhang's memorial settling peace, jealous of Liu Yongfu's daring to fight, speaking with utmost indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Vice Director Pan Yantong secretly submitted five stratagems against the enemy and impeached Li Hongzhang's peace memorial, resenting Liu Yongfu's willingness to fight, with burning indignation.

sentences.zh: 亡何，法果敗盟，侵台灣雞籠，樞臣議和戰未決。

translations.literal: Before long France broke the treaty and invaded Jilong in Taiwan; the Grand Council debated war and peace without decision.
translations.idiomatic: France soon broke the treaty and attacked Jilong in Taiwan; the Grand Council could not decide between war and peace.

sentences.zh: 於是承修再陳三策：「法所恃為援者西貢、東京。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengxiu again set forth three stratagems: "What France relies on for support are Saigon and Tokyo.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu then offered three stratagems: "France relies on Saigon and Tokyo for support."

sentences.zh: 我若師分三路，亟攻越南，彼將自救不暇，策之上也。

translations.literal: If our armies divide into three routes and urgently attack Vietnam, they will be too busy saving themselves—that is the superior stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: If our armies strike Vietnam in three columns, they will be too busy to defend themselves—the best plan."

sentences.zh: 分兵為守，敵至則戰，敵退不追，老師糜餉，利害共之，策之中也。

translations.literal: Divide troops for defense, fight when the enemy comes and do not pursue when they retreat, aging the army and wasting supplies while sharing harm and benefit—that is the middle stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Hold divided forces, fight on contact but do not pursue, aging the army and wasting supplies while sharing risk—that is the middle plan."

sentences.zh: 若慮餉詘運阻，不敢言戰，則其禍不勝言矣，是謂無策。

translations.literal: If one fears short funds and blocked transport and dares not speak of war, the harm is beyond words—that is called having no stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: If fear of funds and transport blocks talk of war, the harm is beyond words—that is no plan at all."

sentences.zh: 」補鴻臚寺卿，充​​總理各國事務大臣。

translations.literal: " He was supplemented as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and served as Minister in the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and served in the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 自此陳說兵事，章凡十三上，多見採納。

translations.literal: From this time he set forth military affairs; in all thirteen memorials were submitted, many of which were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he memorialized on military affairs thirteen times, many of which the court adopted.

sentences.zh: 嗣以中允樊恭煦獲譴，上疏營救，坐鐫秩。

translations.literal: Soon after, when Junior Mentor Fan Gongxu was punished, he memorialized to rescue him and was demoted one grade as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Junior Mentor Fan Gongxu was punished, he memorialized in his defense and was demoted one grade.

sentences.zh: 明年，赴天津佐鴻章與法使巴特納商和約，定新約十款。

translations.literal: The next year he went to Tianjin to assist Hongzhang in negotiating a treaty with the French envoy Patenotre, fixing ten articles of a new treaty.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he went to Tianjin to help Li Hongzhang negotiate with the French envoy Patenotre and fix ten articles of a new treaty.

sentences.zh: 還，乞歸省。

translations.literal: On return he asked to go home to visit his parents.
translations.idiomatic: On return he asked leave to visit his family.

sentences.zh: 未出都，命赴廣西與法使會勘中、越分界，至則單騎出關會法使浦理燮。

translations.literal: Before leaving the capital he was ordered to Guangxi to survey the Sino-Vietnamese boundary with the French envoy; on arrival he went out of the pass alone on horseback to meet the French envoy Pouliche.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving the capital he was ordered to Guangxi to demarcate the border with the French envoy; on arrival he rode out alone to meet Pouliche.

sentences.zh: 浦理燮欲先勘原界，承修據約先欲改正界限，不相下，乃陽以文淵、保樂、海寧歸我，而陰電其駐京使臣，詆承修違約爭執，謂非先勘原界，勢將罷議。

translations.literal: Pouliche wished to survey the original boundary first; Chengxiu, citing the treaty, insisted on correcting the boundary first and would not yield; he openly offered Wenyuan, Baole, and Haining to us, while secretly cabling his minister in Beijing to denounce Chengxiu for breaking the treaty and contending, saying that unless the original boundary was surveyed first, talks would be broken off.
translations.idiomatic: Pouliche wanted to survey the old border first; Chengxiu, citing treaty terms, insisted on correcting the line first; he openly offered Wenyuan, Baole, and Haining to China while secretly cabling Beijing to accuse Chengxiu of breach and warn talks would collapse without surveying the old line first.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不獲已，許之。

translations.literal: The court, having no choice, agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The court, unable to refuse, agreed.

sentences.zh: 承修遂有三難二害之電奏，略言：「附界居民，不願隸法，先勘原界，慮滋事變，難一。

translations.literal: Chengxiu then telegraphed a memorial on three difficulties and two harms, stating in summary: "Border inhabitants do not wish to be subject to France; surveying the original boundary first risks provoking incidents—that is difficulty one.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu telegraphed on three difficulties and two harms: "Border people refuse French rule; surveying the old line first risks unrest—first difficulty."

sentences.zh: 保樂牧馬，游勇獷盛，道路梗阻，難二。

translations.literal: Baole is used for horse pasture; roaming braves are fierce and roads blocked—that is difficulty two.
translations.idiomatic: Baole serves as pasture; roaming braves are fierce and roads impassable—second difficulty."

sentences.zh: 原界碑折，十不存五，巉崗聳巘，瘴雨炎翳，人馬不前，難三。

translations.literal: Original boundary markers are broken, fewer than half remain; steep peaks tower, malarial rain and blazing heat, men and horses cannot advance—that is difficulty three.
translations.idiomatic: Old markers are broken, fewer than half remain; steep peaks, malarial rain and heat, men and horses cannot pass—third difficulty."

sentences.zh: 且原界既勘，彼必颺去，新界奚論？

translations.literal: Moreover, once the original boundary is surveyed, they will surely remove it—what of the new boundary?
translations.idiomatic: Once the old line is surveyed they will erase it—what then of the new boundary?

sentences.zh: 駈驢、文淵俱不可得，關門失險，戰守兩難，害一。

translations.literal: Qulü and Wenyuan cannot both be obtained; the pass loses its strategic advantage, and both defense and offense are difficult—that is harm one.
translations.idiomatic: Losing Qulü and Wenyuan, the pass loses its advantage and both defense and offense become impossible—first harm."

sentences.zh: 文淵既失，北無寸地，關內通商，勢將迫脅，越既不存，粵將焉保？

translations.literal: Once Wenyuan is lost, there is not an inch of land to the north; inland trade will be forced, Vietnam will not survive, and how can Guangdong be preserved?
translations.idiomatic: Lose Wenyuan and the north has no buffer; inland trade will be coerced, Vietnam will not stand, and Guangdong cannot be saved—second harm."

sentences.zh: 害二。

translations.literal: Harm two.
translations.idiomatic: Second harm."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，不省。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the court took no notice.

sentences.zh: 十二年，法人別遣狄隆、狄塞爾來會。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the French separately sent Dillon and Disère to meet.
translations.idiomatic: In 1886 the French sent Dillon and Disère separately to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 適法官達魯倪思海至者蘭，為越人擊殺。

translations.literal: Just then Judge Daruignies, who had reached Zhelan, was killed by Vietnamese.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Judge Daruignies, who had reached Zhelan, was killed by Vietnamese.

sentences.zh: 狄使懼，又恥而諱其事，堅請按圖畫界，朝旨報可。

translations.literal: The Di envoys were afraid and, ashamed, concealed the matter; they firmly asked to demarcate by map, and the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The French envoys were afraid and ashamed and hid the matter; they insisted on demarcating by map, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是首議江平、黃竹、白龍尾各地割隸越。

translations.literal: Thereupon they first proposed ceding Jiangping, Huangzhu, Bailongwei, and other places to Vietnam.
translations.idiomatic: They first proposed ceding Jiangping, Huangzhu, Bailongwei, and other places to Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 承修指圖籍抗爭，狄使不能屈，欲分白龍尾半之左歸我而右歸越。

translations.literal: Chengxiu cited maps and records to contend; the Di envoys could not overcome him and wished to divide Bailongwei, the left half to us and the right to Vietnam.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu cited maps and fought back; the envoys could not prevail and proposed splitting Bailongwei, left to China and right to Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 承修以其地為欽海外戶，法得之則內偪防城，外斷東興、思勒，是無欽、廉也。

translations.literal: Chengxiu said that place was the outer gateway of Qinzhou; if France obtained it they would press inward on Fangcheng and cut off Dongxing and Sile outward—that would mean no Qin or Lian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu said the place was Qinzhou's outer gateway; French possession would press Fangcheng inward and sever Dongxing and Sile—Qin and Lian would be lost.

sentences.zh: 議久之，暫與定約三條，猶未決，而狄使竟以兵力驅江平、黃竹居民內徙。

translations.literal: After long deliberation they temporarily fixed three articles of agreement, still undecided, while the Di envoys used force to drive the inhabitants of Jiangping and Huangzhu to move inward.
translations.idiomatic: Talks lingered; three provisional articles were drafted but unsettled, while French troops drove Jiangping and Huangzhu residents inland.

sentences.zh: 朝廷慮啟邊釁，命先勘欽西至桂省全界，承修遂與訂定清約，語詳邦交志。

translations.literal: The court feared border conflict and ordered survey first from Qinzhou west to the full boundary of Guangxi; Chengxiu then concluded the Qing treaty, detailed in the record of foreign relations.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing border clash, the court ordered survey from Qinzhou west through Guangxi; Chengxiu then concluded the treaty, as detailed in the foreign-relations annals.

sentences.zh: 十三年，具約本末以上，复官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he submitted the full account of the treaty above and was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887 he reported the treaty's full story to the throne and was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 十四年，謝病歸，主講豐湖書院，讀書養母。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he resigned on grounds of illness, became lecturer at Fenghu Academy, and read books while caring for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1888 he retired ill, lectured at Fenghu Academy, and studied while caring for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒於惠州。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died at Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Huizhou in 1891.

sentences.zh: 徐致祥，字季和，江蘇嘉定人。

translations.literal: Xu Zhixiang, styled Jihe, was a native of Jiading in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhixiang, courtesy name Jihe, came from Jiading in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 晉中允，典試山東。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Mentor and conducted the Shandong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Junior Mentor and supervised the Shandong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士，督順天學政。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretary and supervised education in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Secretary and served as educational commissioner for Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 遭憂去，服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning; when mourning ended he resumed his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He left on mourning; when it ended he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，法越構兵，德璀琳以和議進，朝旨未決。
