translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu, when France and Vietnam went to war, Detring advanced peace proposals and the court's edict was undecided.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884, as France and Vietnam fought, Detring urged peace while the court hesitated.

sentences.zh: 致祥上三策，謂：決戰宜速，任將宜專，軍勢宜聯。

translations.literal: Zhixiang submitted three stratagems, saying: decisive battle should be swift, command of generals should be exclusive, and military strength should be united.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang offered three policies: fight swiftly, give generals sole command, and unite military strength.

sentences.zh: 閩事棘，言何璟、張兆棟無幹濟才，而薦楊岳斌、張佩綸堪重任，頗嘉納。

translations.literal: When Fujian affairs were critical, he said He Jing and Zhang Zhaodong lacked capacity for achievement, but recommended Yang Yuebin and Zhang Peilun as fit for heavy responsibility; this was largely praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Fujian was in crisis he said He Jing and Zhang Zhaodong lacked ability but recommended Yang Yuebin and Zhang Peilun for heavy duties; the court largely approved.

sentences.zh: 時議築鐵路，致祥聞而惡之，痛陳八害，並請力辟邪說，亟修河工，上責其誕妄，鐫三級。

translations.literal: At the time railways were debated; on hearing this Zhixiang detested the idea, painfully set forth eight harms, and also asked to forcefully reject heterodox doctrines and urgently repair river works; the throne reproached him for absurdity and demoted him three grades.
translations.idiomatic: When railways were debated he denounced them, listed eight harms, urged rejecting heterodox schemes and repairing rivers; the throne called him absurd and demoted him three grades.

sentences.zh: 越二年，鐵路議再起，又再阻止之。

translations.literal: Two years later the railway debate arose again and he again blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, when railways were debated again, he blocked them again.

sentences.zh: 先後封事十數上，而惓惓於抑奄寺，治河工，為時論所美。

translations.literal: In all more than ten sealed memorials were submitted, while he earnestly pressed suppression of eunuchs and river works—praised in public opinion of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted more than ten sealed memorials, earnestly urging restraint of eunuchs and river repair—praised by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 歷典福建、廣東鄉試。

translations.literal: He successively conducted the Fujian and Guangdong provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Fujian and Guangdong provincial examinations in turn.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授大理寺卿，連劾樞臣禮親王世鐸、山西巡撫阿克達春，而糾彈張之洞尤不遺馀力。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, successively impeaching Grand Councilor Prince Shiduo of Li and Shanxi Governor Akedachun, while impeaching Zhang Zhidong with especial relentlessness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1892 he became Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, impeaching Grand Councilor Prince Shiduo and Shanxi Governor Akedachun, and attacking Zhang Zhidong without relent.

sentences.zh: 尋命視學浙江，有嚴名。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to inspect education in Zhejiang and had a reputation for severity.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to inspect education in Zhejiang and gained a reputation for severity.

sentences.zh: 中日之役，我師敗績，上奕劻、李鴻章誤國狀，請逮葉志超、衛汝貴等寘之法，而畀馮子材、劉永福以征討名號，庶可振國威、作士氣。

translations.literal: In the Sino-Japanese war our army was defeated; he memorialized the errors of Yikuang and Li Hongzhang in harming the state, asked that Ye Zhichao, Wei Rugui, and others be arrested and punished by law, and that Feng Zicai and Liu Yongfu be given titles for campaign and suppression, so that national prestige might be revived and morale raised.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat in the Sino-Japanese War he exposed Yikuang and Li Hongzhang's harm to the state, urged arrest of Ye Zhichao and Wei Rugui, and titles for Feng Zicai and Liu Yongfu to revive prestige and morale.

sentences.zh: 會山東教案起，德使海靖勒罷李秉衡職。

translations.literal: When the Shandong missionary case arose, the German envoy Heinke forced the dismissal of Li Bingheng from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shandong missionary case arose, German envoy Heinke forced Li Bingheng's dismissal.

sentences.zh: 致祥曰：「昔歲罷劉秉璋，今茲罷李秉衡，是朝廷黜陟之大權操之敵人也。

translations.literal: Zhixiang said: "Last year Liu Bingzhang was dismissed; this year Li Bingheng is dismissed—the court's great power of appointment and removal is in the enemy's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang said: "Last year Liu Bingzhang was dismissed; this year Li Bingheng—great appointment power now rests with the enemy."

sentences.zh: 為請顧全國體，毋懾敵。

translations.literal: I ask that national dignity be preserved and the enemy not be feared.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that national dignity be preserved and the court not fear the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」私念國是不振，亂未有已，乃援引聖祖篤信硃子垂為家法往事，請舉行經筵以輔聖德，皆不報。

translations.literal: " Privately he thought the national policy was not revived and disorder had no end; he cited the past when the Kangxi emperor deeply believed in Zhu Xi and made it family law, asking that the classics lecture be held to assist the sage's virtue—all without response.
translations.idiomatic: Privately he thought policy was failing and disorder unending; citing Kangxi's devotion to Zhu Xi as family law, he asked for classics lectures to aid the emperor's virtue—all unanswered.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，還朝，遷兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to court and was transferred to Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned and was made Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，上違豫，眾情驚疑，復以輔導君德之說進。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when the emperor fell ill, public feeling was alarmed and doubtful; he again advanced the proposal to guide the ruler's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898, when the emperor fell ill and public alarm grew, he again urged guidance of the ruler's virtue.

sentences.zh: 是時國家多故，聖嗣尚虛，致祥為重國本計，略言：「昔宋真宗取宗室子養之宮中，逮仁宗既生，即遣歸邸；

translations.literal: At that time the state had many troubles and the imperial heir was still vacant; Zhixiang, planning for the foundation of the state, wrote briefly: "Formerly Song Zhenzong took sons of the imperial clan to rear in the palace; when Renzong was born they were sent back to their residences;
translations.idiomatic: The realm was troubled and the heir still vacant; Zhixiang, weighing the foundation of state, wrote: "Song Zhenzong once reared imperial clansmen in the palace; when Renzong was born they were sent home;"

sentences.zh: 厥後仁宗、高宗、理宗皆踵行之。

translations.literal: Afterward Renzong, Gaozong, and Lizong all followed this practice.
translations.idiomatic: Later Renzong, Gaozong, and Lizong all followed the practice."

sentences.zh: 有子而遣養子歸邸者，真宗是也。

translations.literal: To have a son and send the adopted son back to his residence—that was Zhenzong.
translations.idiomatic: Sending adopted sons home once a natural son was born—that was Zhenzong's case."

sentences.zh: 無子而即以養子傳授神器者，仁宗之於英宗，高宗之於孝宗，理宗之於度宗是也。

translations.literal: To have no son and directly transmit the sacred vessel to the adopted son—that was Renzong to Yingzong, Gaozong to Xiaozong, and Lizong to Duzong.
translations.idiomatic: Transmitting the throne to an adopted son when there was no heir—that was Renzong to Yingzong, Gaozong to Xiaozong, Lizong to Duzong."

sentences.zh: 今以宗社系託之重，臣民屬望之切，深維至計，取則前朝，慎選近支宗室兄弟之子數人，擇親擇賢，入侍禁中，止以為子，不以為儲，恪遵家法，既可默察其賢否，徐以俟皇子之生。

translations.literal: Now, given the weight of entrusting the altars of state and the urgency of officials and people's hopes, deeply weighing the supreme plan and taking the former dynasty as model, carefully select several sons of close-branch imperial clansmen, choose by kinship and choose by worth, enter service in the forbidden quarters, only as sons and not as heir apparent, strictly obey family law—thus their worth may be quietly observed while awaiting the birth of an imperial son in time.
translations.idiomatic: Given the weight of the succession and public expectation, he urged choosing several worthy sons of close imperial clansmen to enter the palace as foster sons but not as heir apparent, per family law, until an imperial son should be born."

sentences.zh: 則皇上未有子而有子，皇太后未有孫而有孫，而穆宗付託之大業，亦繼承有屬矣。

translations.literal: Then though the emperor has no son he would have sons, though the empress dowager has no grandson she would have grandsons, and the great enterprise entrusted by Muzong would also have succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the emperor would have sons in name, the empress dowager grandsons in name, and Tongzhi's entrusted succession would be secured."

sentences.zh: 」乃未幾，果有立溥俊為大阿哥事。

translations.literal: " Before long, indeed, there was the affair of establishing Pujun as the Great Heir.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, indeed, Pujun was established as Great Heir.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1899.

sentences.zh: 論曰：體芳、寶廷、佩綸與張之洞，時稱翰林四諫，有大政事，必具疏論是非，與同時好言事者，又號「清流黨」。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Tifang, Baoting, Peilun, and Zhang Zhidong were at the time called the Four Remonstrators of the Hanlin; on great affairs of state they always submitted memorials debating right and wrong, and with others of the time who liked to speak on affairs were also called the "Pure Stream Party."
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes: Tifang, Baoting, Peilun, and Zhang Zhidong were called the Four Hanlin Remonstrators; on great affairs they memorialized on right and wrong, and with like-minded colleagues were called the Pure Stream Party.

sentences.zh: 然體芳、寶廷議承大統，惓惓忠愛，非佩綸等所能及也。

translations.literal: Yet Tifang and Baoting, in debating succession to the great line, showed earnest loyal love beyond what Peilun and the like could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in debating the imperial succession Tifang and Baoting showed a loyal devotion Peilun and others could not match.

sentences.zh: 承修以搏擊為能，致祥以誕妄受責，君子譏之。

translations.literal: Chengxiu made attack his ability; Zhixiang was punished for absurdity—gentlemen mocked them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu excelled at attack; Zhixiang was punished for absurdity—men of judgment mocked both.

sentences.zh: 唯盛昱言不妄發，潔身早退，庶超然無負清譽歟？

translations.literal: Only Shengyu did not speak rashly, kept himself pure and retired early—perhaps he alone did not betray his reputation for integrity?
translations.idiomatic: Only Shengyu spoke cautiously, lived cleanly, and retired early—perhaps he alone did not betray his reputation for integrity.
